verses.pali: Aṅguttara Nikāya 4.41
verses.english: Numbered Discourses 4.41

verses.pali: 5. Rohitassavagga
verses.english: 5. With Rohitassa

verses.pali: Samādhibhāvanāsutta
verses.english: Ways of Developing Immersion Further

verses.pali: “Catasso imā, bhikkhave, samādhibhāvanā.
verses.english: “Mendicants, there are these four ways of developing immersion further.

verses.pali: Katamā catasso?
verses.english: What four?

verses.pali: Atthi, bhikkhave, samādhibhāvanā bhāvitā bahulīkatā diṭṭhadhammasukhavihārāya saṁvattati;
verses.english: There is a way of developing immersion further that leads to blissful meditation in this life.

verses.pali: atthi, bhikkhave, samādhibhāvanā bhāvitā bahulīkatā ñāṇadassanappaṭilābhāya saṁvattati;
verses.english: There is a way of developing immersion further that leads to gaining knowledge and vision.

verses.pali: atthi, bhikkhave, samādhibhāvanā bhāvitā bahulīkatā satisampajaññāya saṁvattati;
verses.english: There is a way of developing immersion further that leads to mindfulness and awareness.

verses.pali: atthi, bhikkhave, samādhibhāvanā bhāvitā bahulīkatā āsavānaṁ khayāya saṁvattati.
verses.english: There is a way of developing immersion further that leads to the ending of defilements.

verses.pali: Katamā ca, bhikkhave, samādhibhāvanā bhāvitā bahulīkatā diṭṭhadhammasukhavihārāya saṁvattati?
verses.english: And what is the way of developing immersion further that leads to blissful meditation in this life?

verses.pali: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu vivicceva kāmehi …pe… catutthaṁ jhānaṁ upasampajja viharati.
verses.english: It’s when a mendicant, quite secluded from sensual pleasures, secluded from unskillful qualities, enters and remains in the first absorption … second absorption … third absorption … fourth absorption.

verses.pali: Ayaṁ, bhikkhave, samādhibhāvanā bhāvitā bahulīkatā diṭṭhadhammasukhavihārāya saṁvattati.
verses.english: This is the way of developing immersion further that leads to blissful meditation in this life.

verses.pali: Katamā ca, bhikkhave, samādhibhāvanā bhāvitā bahulīkatā ñāṇadassanappaṭilābhāya saṁvattati?
verses.english: And what is the way of developing immersion further that leads to gaining knowledge and vision?

verses.pali: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu ālokasaññaṁ manasi karoti, divāsaññaṁ adhiṭṭhāti—
verses.english: It’s when a mendicant applies their mind to the perception of light, focusing on the perception of day:

verses.pali: yathā divā tathā rattiṁ, yathā rattiṁ tathā divā.
verses.english: as by day, so by night; as by night, so by day.

verses.pali: Iti vivaṭena cetasā apariyonaddhena sappabhāsaṁ cittaṁ bhāveti.
verses.english: And so, with an open and unenveloped heart, they develop a mind that’s full of radiance.

verses.pali: Ayaṁ, bhikkhave, samādhibhāvanā bhāvitā bahulīkatā ñāṇadassanappaṭilābhāya saṁvattati.
verses.english: This is the way of developing immersion further that leads to gaining knowledge and vision.

verses.pali: Katamā ca, bhikkhave, samādhibhāvanā bhāvitā bahulīkatā satisampajaññāya saṁvattati?
verses.english: And what is the way of developing immersion further that leads to mindfulness and awareness?

verses.pali: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno viditā vedanā uppajjanti, viditā upaṭṭhahanti, viditā abbhatthaṁ gacchanti;
verses.english: It’s when a mendicant knows feelings as they arise, as they remain, and as they go away.

verses.pali: viditā saññā …pe… viditā vitakkā uppajjanti, viditā upaṭṭhahanti, viditā abbhatthaṁ gacchanti.
verses.english: They know perceptions as they arise, as they remain, and as they go away. They know thoughts as they arise, as they remain, and as they go away.

verses.pali: Ayaṁ, bhikkhave, samādhibhāvanā bhāvitā bahulīkatā satisampajaññāya saṁvattati.
verses.english: This is the way of developing immersion further that leads to mindfulness and awareness.

verses.pali: Katamā ca, bhikkhave, samādhibhāvanā bhāvitā bahulīkatā āsavānaṁ khayāya saṁvattati?
verses.english: And what is the way of developing immersion further that leads to the ending of defilements?

verses.pali: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu pañcasu upādānakkhandhesu udayabbayānupassī viharati:
verses.english: It’s when a mendicant meditates observing rise and fall in the five grasping aggregates.

verses.pali: ‘iti rūpaṁ, iti rūpassa samudayo, iti rūpassa atthaṅgamo;
verses.english: ‘Such is form, such is the origin of form, such is the ending of form.

verses.pali: iti vedanā, iti vedanāya samudayo, iti vedanāya atthaṅgamo;
verses.english: Such is feeling, such is the origin of feeling, such is the ending of feeling.

verses.pali: iti saññā, iti saññāya samudayo, iti saññāya atthaṅgamo;
verses.english: Such is perception, such is the origin of perception, such is the ending of perception.

verses.pali: iti saṅkhārā, iti saṅkhārānaṁ samudayo, iti saṅkhārānaṁ atthaṅgamo;
verses.english: Such are choices, such is the origin of choices, such is the ending of choices.

verses.pali: iti viññāṇaṁ, iti viññāṇassa samudayo, iti viññāṇassa atthaṅgamo’ti.
verses.english: Such is consciousness, such is the origin of consciousness, such is the ending of consciousness.’

verses.pali: Ayaṁ, bhikkhave, samādhibhāvanā bhāvitā bahulīkatā āsavānaṁ khayāya saṁvattati.
verses.english: This is the way of developing immersion further that leads to the ending of defilements.

verses.pali: Imā kho, bhikkhave, catasso samādhibhāvanā.
verses.english: These are the four ways of developing immersion further.

verses.pali: Idañca pana metaṁ, bhikkhave, sandhāya bhāsitaṁ pārāyane puṇṇakapañhe:
verses.english: And it was in this connection that I said in ‘The Way to the Far Shore’, in ‘The Questions of Puṇṇaka’:

verses.pali: ‘Saṅkhāya lokasmiṁ paroparāni,
verses.english: ‘Having appraised the world high and low,

verses.pali: Yassiñjitaṁ natthi kuhiñci loke;
verses.english: there is nothing in the world that disturbs them.

verses.pali: Santo vidhūmo anīgho nirāso,
verses.english: Peaceful, unclouded, untroubled, <j>with no need for hope,

verses.pali: Atāri so jātijaranti brūmī’”ti.
verses.english: they’ve crossed over rebirth and old age, I declare.’”

verses.pali: Paṭhamaṁ.
